scores.claim_text: Definitive Merger Agreement (2024-12-22) with Norse Holdings / Navy Acquisition Co. (Family + Liverpool) at $24.25/share cash.
scores.M_value: Norse Holdings: 20 hits including 8-K 2024-12-23 (announcement), 8-Ks in 2025-04, 2025-05-09, 2025-05-16, 2025-05-19, 2025-05-20 (closing-cadence). Navy Acquisition: 24 hits same pattern. 'Liverpool' in JWN-only filings: 22 hits.
scores.interpretation: Merger Agreement existence and counterparty identity are fully corroborated by JWN's own 8-K filing cadence. Critical: the 2025-05 8-K cluster (filed 2025-05-09, 2025-05-16, 2025-05-19, 2025-05-20 — straddling the cutoff date 2026-05-16) is consistent with merger consummation/closing milestones immediately before/around cutoff. This is a take-private TRANSACTION risk profile (deal-break risk / regulatory-approval risk / financing risk), not a financial-distress profile. Calibration Heuristic 10 (delisting/going-concern) does NOT apply in the distress sense — JWN exits public markets at a premium, not via Form 15/25-NSE due to operating failure. PASS as a verified disclosure; the residual risk is deal-break, which is asymmetrically rewarded (event-driven, not the framework's distress thesis).

scores.claim_text: Total Company comparable sales +3.6% FY2024; Nordstrom banner comp +3% (Q4 over +5%); net sales $14,557M (+2.4%); Retail-segment EBIT $872M.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext for 'comparable sales' cik=JWN (cross-check across 10-K + quarterly 8-K earnings reports + 10-Q)
scores.M_value: 14 hits — quarterly earnings 8-K cadence (Q1 2024-05-30, Q2 2024-08-27, Q3 2024-11-26, Q4 2025-03-04) plus 10-Qs (2024-06, 2024-09) consistently disclose comparable-sales metric. Q4 8-K (2025-03-04) and full-year 10-K (2025-03-21) figures internally consistent (positive comp directionality confirmed across each quarter).
scores.interpretation: Comp-sales claim survives Calibration Heuristic 9 test — marketing-tier positive comp (+3.6%) is reconciled to financial-statement net-sales growth (+2.4% reported, +130bps from 53rd-week roll-off, normalized ~+3.7%) and segment EBIT improvement ($855M -> $872M). There is no gap between marketing-tier and financial-statement-tier comp directionality. Retail segment EBIT margin (Retail segment EBIT $872M / segment sales $14,557M = 6.0%) is consistent with mid-tier department store. PASS. Note: Q4 +5% Nordstrom-banner comp suggests Rack drove the full-year comp lower (since Rack had openings without proportional sales growth) — consistent with disclosed 23 new Rack stores.

scores.claim_text: Store fleet 386 (9 SCN + 98 Nordstrom + 279 Rack) at 2025-02-01; FY2024: 23 Rack openings, 6 total closures; FY2025: 20 Rack openings + 1 Nordstrom closure announced.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext 'Nordstrom' cik=SPG (Simon, 0001063761) and cik=MAC (Macerich, 0000912242) — mall REITs disclose top-tenant exposure.
scores.M_value: SPG: 22 hits in filings 2023-02-23 -> 2026-02-25 (every annual 10-K through current — Nordstrom remains a named tenant disclosed in SPG 10-K through 2026). MAC: 33 hits across 10-Ks and 8-Ks including 2026-05-06 8-K and 2026-02-18 8-K — Macerich continues to reference Nordstrom into 2026.
scores.interpretation: Counterparty corroboration is STRONG. Both major mall-REIT landlords (SPG and MAC) name Nordstrom in their 10-Ks every year through fiscal 2026, including in 2026-Q1 8-Ks dated AFTER the announced merger and right up to cutoff. This is the opposite of a 'tenant-vacate' signal — Nordstrom is operationally INTACT as a mall anchor through cutoff. Combined with the disclosed FY2024 store-count INCREASE (368->386) and announced FY2025 net additions (Rack-led growth), Calibration Heuristic 11 (store-count trajectory) and Heuristic 3 (planned vs. operational) both PASS. JWN is operationally not a closure story; it is a take-private story. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Nordstrom credit-card program with TD (amended Oct-2024 to transition customer-facing functions to TD). Credit-card revenues $459M (2024) vs $474M (2023) vs $438M (2022).
scores.M_value: TD: 3 hits — 40-F (2024-12-06), 40-F/A (2024-12-09), 40-F (2025-12-04). Counterparty annual reports both before and after the program-amendment date acknowledge Nordstrom.
scores.interpretation: TD's 40-F filings name Nordstrom in both the year of the program amendment (FY2024 fiscal-year-end Oct 2024 = filed Dec 2024) and the subsequent year (filed Dec 2025), confirming the program agreement remains live through cutoff. Credit-card revenue decline YoY (-$15M, -3.2%) is modest and reverses the +$36M rebuild from 2022->2023; in context of the program-economics renegotiation it's a soft margin signal but not a covenant or break event. PASS — counterparty disclosure verified, no contradiction. Calibration: this is the type of slow-bleed dynamic flagged in the cohort calibration note.

scores.claim_text: Nordstrom Canada CCAA wind-down commenced 2023-03-02 and was substantially completed by FY2023 year-end; ASOS|Nordstrom JV also exited Dec 2023.
scores.M_value: 'Canada wind-down': 17 hits, 'CCAA': 12 hits. Hits span 2023 8-Ks (2023-05-31, 2023-08-24) and 10-Qs (Q1 2023-06-07, Q2 2023-09-01, Q3 2023-12-01), with discussion continuing into 2024-2025 10-K filings (Note 2 referenced).
scores.interpretation: Past distress event that has been EXECUTED, not just announced — passes Calibration Heuristic 3 (planned-vs-operational). The CCAA filing is a real Calibration Heuristic 10 distress marker but the post-wind-down accounting (deconsolidation, charges taken in 2023) is now in the rear-view mirror. By cutoff 2026-05-16 this is a closed chapter and does not signal forward distress. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Nordstrom is a wholesale customer of major apparel/accessories suppliers including VF Corp, Tapestry, Hanesbrands, Levi Strauss. (Implicit channel-disclosure test.)
scores.M_value: VFC: 1 hit (DEF 14A 2025-06-09, likely director-bio context). TPR: 0 hits. HBI: 0 hits. LEVI: 8 hits all in DEF 14A 2023/2026 — proxy not 10-K customer disclosure.
scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 7 (counterparty-disclosure threshold) test: none of the four named apparel suppliers names Nordstrom in their 10-Ks as a material/10%-concentration customer. This is the EXPECTED outcome — Nordstrom at $14.6B revenue is well below the threshold at which any single major brand would have >10% concentration to Nordstrom (the heuristic explicitly cites Walmart as the comparison case). Absence here is not a hard contradiction; it's expected, and JWN's filing also does NOT claim that any single supplier is a material concentration. The lack of mutual counterparty corroboration is consistent with the department-store mid-tier channel scale, not with a fabricated relationship. PASS.

scores.claim_text: CFO Catherine R. Smith departure announced via 8-K filed 2025-03-04, last day ~2025-03-21. PEO Erik Nordstrom serves as both principal executive officer and the 10-K cover-page filer.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext 'Catherine Smith' cik=JWN + local check of 8-K accession 0001213900-25-019760 (filed 2025-03-04).
scores.M_value: Edgar fulltext returns 1 hit (the 10-K disclosure of her departure). Direct grep of the 2025-03-04 8-K confirms both 'Catherine' and 'resignation' tokens — corroborating the event. The 8-K predates the 10-K filing date (2025-03-21) by 17 days.
scores.interpretation: Verified event. Calibration: CFO departure 4 days before annual reporting deadline and 10 weeks after a definitive go-private signing is a governance event with moderate severity. Three plausible reads: (a) routine pre-close transition / non-renewal; (b) economic incentive — CFO's change-in-control compensation triggers at the closing; (c) less benign — internal disagreement on disclosure / valuation. In the take-private context (where the Family-Group buyer controls the inside view), an exiting CFO loses the standard whistleblower channel. MODE: not a falsification of any specific operating claim, but a soft governance flag. Reduces confidence in unrelated management commentary but does not invalidate any specific verifiable disclosure here.
